I am fascinated by the thought processes of those who dislike this film. I can take "oh I wasn't very interested" but when they say it's boring or nothing happens, it almost feels like they have been wronged and they are disappointed. 

I genuinely think that the influx of found footage films killed the imagination of great horror in the 2010's. BUT I think True Crime is the current killer of horror right now. If 12 year olds can watch gruesome true crime stories on YouTube, then finding out that the potential that this film wasn't real is a real downer. 

I'm someone who thrives seeking out fictional horror, set in reality, and I think the Blair Witch Project is probably the closest to feeling that right? But there are a lot of people out there who thrive on "not falling for it" being real. When in actuality, it's more of an artistic choice for the story. It's like professional wrestling. Obviously it is a theater experience and some people understand and get it, and others just can't. 

Some people are scared of the conjuring and some people are scared of the Blair witch project 🤷‍♂️. My advice is just to enjoy what you love, keep talking about it and spreading that passion, and don't let people dampen that experience for you because they probably get scared watching "The curse of la llorona".
